issues.legal_issue: A transferee is not a member of the undivided family owning a dwelling house merely because the transferee is related by blood to the family through a common ancestor.
material_facts: The dwelling house belonged to the undivided family of the deceased co-owner whose heirs held the property.
The transferee was related by blood to the other co-owners through a common ancestor, but was not a member of the undivided family that owned the dwelling house.
issues.conclusion: The transferee was not a member of the family to which the dwelling house belonged and was therefore an outsider for the purposes of Section 4 of the Partition Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Partition Act refers to a dwelling house belonging to an undivided family and a transferee who is not a member of such family; “such family” means the family that owns the dwelling house. Although the term “family” is to be construed liberally, relationship by blood through a common ancestor does not by itself make a person a member of the owning family. The Court applied the statutory wording and distinguished the authorities cited on family membership, including Kshirode Chunder Ghosal v. Saroda Prosad Mitra and Paluni Del v. Rathi Mallick.

predicates.partition_preemption_proceeding: A proceeding concerns a co-sharer’s claim to purchase a transferred share in a dwelling house belonging to an undivided family.
predicates.dwelling_house_owned_by_undivided_family: The dwelling house is owned by an undivided family.
predicates.transferee_not_member_of_owning_family: The transferee is not a member of the undivided family that owns the dwelling house, even if related by blood through a common ancestor.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption proceeding concerns a dwelling house owned by an undivided family and the transferee is not a member of that owning family, the transferee is an outsider.

issues.legal_issue: A co-sharer may exercise the statutory right to purchase a stranger’s share in an undivided family dwelling house only when the stranger seeks actual partition and separation and possession of that share.
material_facts: The transferee acquired a share in the dwelling house and was a party to the partition suit.
In the written statements and evidence, the transferee asserted his share but did not ask for partition or demand separation and possession of it.
The other co-sharers sought to purchase the transferee’s share under Section 4 of the Partition Act.
issues.conclusion: Because the transferee had not sought partition or separation and possession of his share, the co-sharers’ application to purchase it was premature and had to be dismissed. The co-sharers could apply under Section 4 if the transferee later sought partition and separation and possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Partition Act applies where a share in a dwelling house belonging to an undivided family is transferred to a non-member and the transferee sues for partition. Under Ghantesher Ghosh v. Madan Mohan Ghosh, the statutory conditions must be met, and the right may arise at any stage, including execution, if the transferee seeks separation and possession. A mere assertion of a share is not a demand for partition. Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act protects the family from an outsider’s joint possession, while Section 4 provides the purchase right only when its conditions are fulfilled. The Court agreed with Babu Lal v. Hablnoor Khan that a view allowing pre-emption without the stranger seeking partition conflicts with Ghantesher Ghosh.

rule.if: partition_suit and undivided_family_dwelling_house and outsider_transferee and co_sharer_offers_to_purchase and not transferee_seeks_separation_and_possession

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit for partition of property that includes a dwelling house.
predicates.undivided_family_dwelling_house: The dwelling house belongs to an undivided family.
predicates.outsider_transferee: A person who is not a member of the owning family has acquired a share in the dwelling house.
predicates.co_sharer_offers_to_purchase: A family co-sharer undertakes to purchase the outsider’s share.
predicates.transferee_seeks_separation_and_possessi: The transferee asks, in the suit or in execution proceedings, for actual division and separation and possession of the transferee’s share.

issues.definition: In a partition suit involving an outsider’s share in an undivided family dwelling house, a co-sharer’s offer to purchase does not make statutory pre-emption available unless the outsider seeks separation and possession of the share.
